signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Oil Supply Pressure
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.466, advancing above its SMA20 of 9.363 and SMA50 of 9.402 while holding below the SMA200 at 9.489. The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard flags a strong bilateral divergence, with USD gaining +0.554% across 9 pairs while NOK drops −1.185% across 2 pairs, creating a 1.739% spread that exceeds the critical threshold. WTI crude oil falling to $89.60 per barrel compounds pressure on the energy-linked krone, offsetting NOK's restrictive real policy rate of +1.82%. The Fed at 4.00% vs Norges Bank at 4.50% leaves a 50bp nominal rate deficit for the dollar, but broad greenback outperformance and commodity headwinds dominate the cross. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK, supported by G10 momentum divergence and commodity weakness. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 13:30 UTC. Risk: WTI crude rebounds sharply above $92.00, relieving downside pressure on NOK.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention-Driven Repricing + Carry Tension
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.18, maintaining a position above its SMA20 (157.96) and SMA50 (157.30) while capping below the SMA200 (158.56). Official data confirms Tokyo conducted a record $50 billion single-day intervention to defend the yen, establishing direct policy intervention rather than safe-haven flow as the primary driver of JPY strength. This policy action overlays a backdrop where Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% maintains a 275bp rate differential favoring USD, alongside a +269bp SOFR-TONA OIS carry advantage. FX options reflect extreme hedging demand with 1M 25d Risk Reversals at −1.97 (strong put skew) and IV running at 6.9% vs HV30 of 4.8% (VRP +2.1%). Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY, balancing 275bp carry against active intervention risk. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions at 23:50 UTC. Risk: USD/JPY breaks above 160.00, forcing secondary intervention from Tokyo.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + Persistent ESI Misses
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5597, remaining locked below its SMA20 (0.5639), SMA50 (0.5696), and SMA200 (0.5825) in a established downtrend. Leveraged funds hold a net short position of −23,350 contracts (pctl 21), maintaining a net short bias despite the OIS market pricing an hawkish bias for the RBNZ. Fundamental support remains undermined by the Economic Surprise Index, where NZD registers a strong negative −25.1 rating reflecting persistent data misses. A 125bp carry advantage (Fed 4.00% vs RBNZ 2.75%) continues to favor USD, reinforcing the structural weakness in the pair. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, driven by weak domestic economic surprises and carry disadvantage. Catalyst: RBNZ Governor Orr speech at 22:00 UTC. Risk: RBNZ delivers an unexpectedly hawkish policy signal, triggering a short-covering rally.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Volatility Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1168, positioned below its SMA20 (1.1195), SMA50 (1.1347), and SMA200 (1.1550) within a firm downtrend structure. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds heavily net short EUR at −104,030 contracts, reaching a 52-week percentile extreme of 2% (z = −1.80). Options markets price 1M ATM IV at 5.7% against HV30 of 4.4%, generating a +1.3% Volatility Risk Premium with 25d Risk Reversals showing a mild put skew at −0.33. The Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% provides a 135bp rate advantage to the dollar (+148bp on SOFR-eSTR OIS basis), limiting sustained EUR recovery. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish EUR/USD, constrained by crowded positioning and rate differentials. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Stalled net short additions trigger a short-squeeze back toward the 1.1195 SMA20 level.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Rates Neutrality + Technical MA Compression
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3387, hovering near its SMA20 (1.3348) while remaining capped beneath the SMA50 (1.3363) and SMA200 (1.3425). Central bank policy rates present a neutral spread with both the Fed and BoE set at 4.00% (0bp nominal spread), while OIS SOFR-SONIA pricing shows a marginal +19bp carry preference for USD. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold a net long position of +32,686 contracts (65th percentile), while Economic Surprise data shows GBP at a moderate positive +6.3 index level. The technical moving average cluster between 1.3348 and 1.3363 defines immediate intraday support and resistance. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD, anchored by balanced policy rates and technical compression. Catalyst: BoE Governor Bailey speech at 17:25 UTC. Risk: A breakout beyond the 1.3348/1.3363 technical band driven by US inflation data.
